summary: Proofread + factual + visual audit of CSOAI framework/regulator/globe pages

factual_risks: LINE 53 — WRONG DATE ATTRIBUTION. The amber countdown reads 'EU AI Act GPAI + Art. 50 transparency enforceable (2 Aug 2026)'. GPAI (general-purpose AI model) obligations under Chapter V became applicable on 2 AUGUST 2025, not 2026 — they are already in force. What actually starts on 2 August 2026 is the Act's general application, high-risk systems under Annex III, and Article 50 transparency obligations. CORRECT FIX: drop 'GPAI' from the 2026 countdown (e.g. 'High-risk (Annex III) + Art. 50 transparency obligations apply — 2 Aug 2026'); if you want to mention GPAI, note it has been live since 2 Aug 2025. Note: only GPAI models placed on market BEFORE 2 Aug 2025 have a 2 Aug 2027 compliance deadline.

LINE 54 — LIKELY FABRICATED DATE. The second countdown claims 'Art. 50 AI-content marking (2 Dec 2026)'. There is no 2 December 2026 milestone in the EU AI Act. Article 50 transparency obligations — including the marking/labelling of AI-generated or manipulated content (Art. 50(2) and 50(4)) — apply from 2 AUGUST 2026, the same date as the first countdown. CORRECT FIX: remove this second countdown (it duplicates 2 Aug 2026) or, if you want a distinct GPAI code-of-practice reference, cite the correct instrument — do not invent a December date.

LINES 3-6, 22, 37, 49 — OVERCLAIM: all 13 are called 'global AI-governance frameworks'. Only the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001 (and partly China TC260) are AI-specific governance frameworks. GDPR is data protection; ISO 27001 / SOC 2 / PCI DSS are information-security/trust; HIPAA is health-data privacy; DORA is financial ICT operational resilience; NIS2 is network-and-information-systems cybersecurity; CRA is product cybersecurity; MiCA is crypto-asset regulation. CORRECT FIX: describe the set as 'AI-governance and adjacent compliance frameworks' or 'AI, security, and data-protection frameworks' — accurate and still impressive. The Dataset JSON-LD description (line 37) has the same overclaim and is what answer engines will cite verbatim.

LINE 23 — OVERSIMPLIFICATION: FAQ calls 2 Aug 2026 'the 2 August 2026 enforcement date' (singular/definite). The EU AI Act applies on a STAGGERED schedule: prohibited practices + AI literacy from 2 Feb 2025; GPAI obligations from 2 Aug 2025; high-risk (Annex III) + Art. 50 transparency from 2 Aug 2026; high-risk under Annex I (product safety) + pre-existing GPAI models from 2 Aug 2027. CORRECT FIX: '…ahead of the 2 August 2026 milestone, when high-risk (Annex III) and Art. 50 transparency obligations apply.'

LINE 22 vs rest — INCONSISTENT COUNT: FAQ says '13+' frameworks while the title (line 30), hero (line 49) and Dataset (line 37) all say exactly 13, and the FRAMEWORKS array (line 8) contains exactly 13. The '+' implies undisclosed extra coverage. CORRECT FIX: say '13' everywhere, or list the additional frameworks the '+' refers to.

LINE 15 — LOW-PRIORITY INDICATIVE MAPPING: 'MiCA Art. 68' is mapped to Security & resilience. MiCA Art. 68 governs operating rules and systems/security of crypto trading platforms; MiCA's substantive ICT-resilience requirements largely defer to DORA. Fine as an indicative pointer given the on-page disclaimer, but verify before any legal-facing use.
proof_fixes: The other 30+ article citations in the matrix check out and are a genuine strength — spot-verified: EU AI Act Art. 9 (risk mgmt), Art. 10 (data), Art. 13/50 (transparency), Art. 14 (oversight), Art. 15 (security), Art. 11-12/Annex IV (docs); DORA Art. 5-6/9/28-RoI; NIS2 Art. 20/21; GDPR Art. 5-6/13-14/22; ISO 27001:2022 A.5-A.8 (all four theme groups); SOC 2 CC1/CC2; NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.11; ISO 42001 6.1/8.2 all correct. Keep them.

Line 37 Dataset license is 'https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT' — MIT is a software license, not a data license. For a crawlable Dataset use a Creative Commons license (e.g. CC-BY-4.0) so the 'open/citable' claim is technically coherent.
Line 8 code comment and Dataset keywords repeat 'ISO 42001' while the visible table uses the correct full name 'ISO/IEC 42001'. Normalise to 'ISO/IEC 42001' everywhere for citation accuracy.

Line 30 document.title and line 49 hero both hard-code '13 frameworks' — if the framework list ever grows, these three literals (title, hero, Dataset) plus the '13+' in FAQ drift out of sync. Consider deriving the count from FRAMEWORKS.length.

Disclaimer on line 84 ('References are indicative … not legal advice … Verify against primary sources') is well done and should stay — but it does not cover the two enforcement-date errors above, which read as authoritative countdowns, not indicative mappings. Fix the dates rather than relying on the disclaimer.

factual_risks: WRONG ADOPTION DATE (lines 111-113, 431-432): page states the AI Act was 'Adopted on July 12, 2024' and that on 'July 12, 2024 ... European Parliament formally adopted the AI Act.' CORRECT: the European Parliament adopted the Act on 13 March 2024 and the Council formally adopted it on 21 May 2024. 12 July 2024 is the date it was PUBLISHED in the Official Journal (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) — the Parliament took no vote on that date. Relabel the 12 July milestone 'Published in the Official Journal' and fix the hero sentence to say adopted March/May 2024, published 12 July 2024, in force 1 August 2024.

WRONG LIMITED-RISK DEADLINE (line 84): Limited Risk / transparency is dated 'August 2, 2025.' CORRECT: the Article 50 transparency obligations (chatbots, deepfakes, AI-generated content) apply from 2 August 2026, the general application date — NOT 2025. Only the prohibitions/AI-literacy (2 Feb 2025) and GPAI + governance + penalties (2 Aug 2025) apply earlier. Change the Limited Risk badge to 'August 2, 2026.'

OVERSTATED DATA OBLIGATION (line 207): 'Training data must be relevant, representative, and error-free.' CORRECT: Article 10(3) requires datasets be 'relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete.' The Act does NOT mandate absolute error-free data; 'error-free' overstates the legal standard. Reword to '...and, to the best extent possible, free of errors.'

UNCITED / MISLABELLED COUNT (lines 278, 859): 'all 113 EU AI Act requirements' and '113 Requirements Covered.' The figure 113 is the number of ARTICLES in Regulation 2024/1689, not a count of discrete 'requirements.' Presenting the article count as a requirements count is unsupported. Say '113 Articles' or drop the precise number.

DIGITAL OMNIBUS DATE (lines 148, 337): 'proposed November 26, 2025.' The European Commission presented the Digital Omnibus package on 19 November 2025, not 26 November. Verify against the Commission press release and correct to 19 November 2025 (the section badge 'November 2025' is fine).

INCOMPLETE HIGH-RISK DEADLINE in FAQ (line 317): 'For high-risk AI systems, you have until August 2026 to achieve full compliance.' Incomplete: high-risk systems that are safety components of products regulated under Annex I (e.g. medical devices, machinery) have until 2 August 2027 (Art. 113(c)). Add the Annex I / 2027 carve-out so the answer isn't misleading for product manufacturers.

factual_risks: 'NIST AI RMF Cyber AI Profile' is presented as a finalized 'New Release - December 2025' (lines 254, 421, 453, 779) with definitive claims ('provides explicit mappings between the two frameworks'). CORRECT FACT: as of the Jan 2026 cutoff, NIST's Cyber AI Profile is an in-development effort led by the NCCoE — a concept paper (released ~2025) plus workshops/public comment — NOT a published final profile. Presenting a draft/concept effort as a released, mappings-complete document is an overclaim. Reword to 'a draft Cyber AI Profile is in development (concept paper released 2025, public comment ongoing)' unless a final publication with an exact NIST publication number can be cited.

GOVERN categories are scrambled/misattributed vs AI RMF 1.0. The page OMITS the real GOVERN 6 (third-party / supply-chain risk) entirely and instead labels GV-5 'Risk Management Integration' and GV-6 'Stakeholder Engagement' (lines 58–67). CORRECT FACT per NIST AI RMF 1.0: GOVERN 4 = organizational safety-first culture (not 'Organizational Context'), GOVERN 5 = robust stakeholder/AI-actor engagement, GOVERN 6 = policies for third-party software/data supply-chain risk. Fix GV-4/5/6 to match, and restore the supply-chain category.

MAP 4 is mislabeled 'Risk Tolerance' (lines 96–98). CORRECT FACT: in AI RMF 1.0, MAP 4 covers risks and benefits mapped for all AI-system components including third-party software/data. 'Risk tolerance' is a GOVERN concept (GOVERN 1.3), not a MAP category — relabel MP-4.

MANAGE 3 is mislabeled 'Risk Monitoring' (lines 160–162). CORRECT FACT: MANAGE 3 in AI RMF 1.0 addresses AI risks and benefits from third parties being managed; ongoing monitoring is folded into MANAGE 4. Relabel MG-3 to the third-party dimension (matching the omitted supply-chain theme above).

OECD alignment claim 'The AI RMF was developed in consultation with OECD' (line 313). CORRECT FACT: NIST developed the AI RMF via a congressionally-directed (National AI Initiative Act of 2020), open multi-stakeholder process; it ALIGNS with and includes a crosswalk to the OECD AI Principles, but 'developed in consultation with OECD' overstates OECD's role. Reword to 'aligns with, and includes an official crosswalk to, the OECD AI Principles.'

factual_risks: '4 Informative Annexes' (line 501) and 'four informative annexes' (line 673) are WRONG. In ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Annex A ('Reference control objectives and controls', lines 314-315) is NORMATIVE — it is the mandatory control reference audited for certification. Only Annexes B, C and D are informative. Correct: '4 annexes — Annex A normative, Annexes B–D informative.' Calling the audited control set 'informative' is a material governance error on an authority page.

The 'five domains' framing of Annex A is inaccurate. Quick-stat implies it, and FAQ line 424 plus Annex A categories (lines 317-323) list exactly five buckets. Annex A of ISO/IEC 42001:2023 actually contains ~38 controls organised under NINE control objectives (A.2–A.10): Policies related to AI; Internal organization; Resources for AI systems; Assessing impacts of AI systems; AI system life cycle; Data for AI systems; Information for interested parties; Use of AI systems; Third-party & customer relationships. Replace the invented 'five domains' with the real 9 control objectives / ~38 controls.

The entire 'Recent Certifications' block (lines 229-272) states specific certification bodies and 'first'-superlatives with NO citations — honesty-critical. 'Microsoft … First major cloud provider certified' (line 235) is contestable: AWS and others also hold ISO 42001, and Anthropic (certified via Schellman) was among the very first AI developers certified. 'KPMG … First Big Four firm certified' (line 240), the CB attributions (BSI/LRQA/Schellman/TÜV) and 2024/2025 dates are all unverified. Either cite each company's certificate/press release inline or remove the section — unsourced 'first' claims about named firms are the highest-risk content here.

Line 1085: 'NIST AI RMF — The US framework that maps directly to ISO 42001 structure' is an overclaim. NIST AI RMF is organised around four functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) and does NOT map directly onto ISO 42001's Annex SL clause structure (Clauses 4–10). They are complementary and commonly cross-walked, not structurally aligned. Reword to 'a complementary US framework often cross-walked to ISO 42001', not 'maps directly'.

FAQ line 408 'Article 40 of the EU AI Act explicitly mentions harmonized standards' is correct (Art. 40 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 covers harmonised standards) — but 'ISO 42001 is expected to become a key supporting standard' is optimistic: CEN-CENELEC is drafting dedicated EU harmonised standards under the AI Act mandate, and ISO 42001 is not confirmed as THE harmonised standard. Keep it clearly hedged as 'may support', not presumed.

Certification-timeline durations (lines 125-190: 'Stage 1 Audit 1-2 days', 'Stage 2 Audit 2-5 days', '6-12 months' etc.) are presented as fact but uncited. They are plausible industry norms — lower risk — but should be framed as 'typical/illustrative' and ideally sourced, since they read as authoritative.

Line 28 eyebrow 'active enforcement 2026': DORA has APPLIED since 17 Jan 2025; 'active enforcement' is defensible but soften to 'applicable since Jan 2025 · under supervision 2026' to avoid implying a distinct 2026 enforcement start.

factual_risks: THE '~65% overlap with NIS2' STAT IS UNCITED AND HAS NO AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE (lines 4, 17, 18, 30 — stated 4 times, including as a hard '65%'). There is no ESA/Commission/ENISA publication quantifying the DORA–NIS2 overlap at 65%. CORRECT FACT: The relationship is qualitative and governed by lex specialis — under NIS2 Article 4 and Recital 28, where a sector-specific Union act (DORA) imposes ICT-risk/incident-reporting requirements at least equivalent to NIS2, the DORA provisions apply IN PLACE OF the corresponding NIS2 ones for financial entities. Fix: drop the precise percentage and say 'DORA is lex specialis to NIS2 for financial entities — its ICT-risk and incident-reporting rules displace the equivalent NIS2 obligations' (cite NIS2 Art. 4 / DORA Recital 16).

MISLEADING FRAMING on line 17: 'For entities in scope of both, mapping the overlap once avoids duplicated controls.' Because DORA is lex specialis (see above), financial entities are largely NOT subject to NIS2's substantive ICT requirements at all — DORA replaces them rather than stacking on top. CORRECT FACT: The value proposition is not 'you're double-regulated, map once' but 'DORA supersedes NIS2's ICT obligations for you; we confirm which NIS2 duties (if any, e.g. as an essential/important entity in a non-financial capacity) still bite.' Reframe to avoid implying dual substantive compliance.

Line 16 'several national deadlines have already passed and consolidation at the ESAs is under way' — vague and slightly off. CORRECT FACT: The Register of Information is not set by staggered 'national deadlines'; financial entities submitted their RoI to their competent authority in a coordinated EU exercise in April 2025 (following the 2024 ESA dry run), for onward consolidation by the ESAs. Replace 'several national deadlines have already passed' with the specific April 2025 first-collection milestone.

factual_risks: WRONG DATE (most serious): The page states the NIS2 transposition deadline is 'October 2026' (line 30 H1 subtext, line 5 code comment, line 15 FAQ 'transposition deadline in October 2026'). CORRECT FACT: the NIS2 transposition deadline was 17 October 2024, with entities required to apply measures from 18 October 2024 (Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Art. 41). As of July 2026 that deadline is nearly two years past — several member states transposed late, but the legal deadline is 2024, not 2026. For a compliance vendor this is a credibility-critical error. Replace with '17 October 2024' and note that national implementation is still being completed in some states.

FABRICATED/UNVERIFIABLE SPECIFIC CLAIM: Line 5 (comment) and lines 9, 15, 16, 18 reference 'common incident-reporting templates adopted May 2026' / 'the Cooperation Group adopted common incident-reporting templates (26 May 2026)'. CORRECT FACT: there is no widely-sourced record of a Cooperation Group common reporting template adopted on 26 May 2026. The real, citable instrument is Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 of 17 October 2024, which sets the technical/methodological requirements and defines when an incident is 'significant' for specific entity types (DNS, cloud, data centres, MSPs, etc.). Remove the 26 May 2026 claim or replace it with a citation to IR (EU) 2024/2690; do not present an unverifiable dated event as fact.

UNCITED / INVENTED STATISTIC: 'Overlaps DORA by ~65%' (line 6 comment, line 17 FAQ 'overlap by roughly 65% on ICT risk management, incident reporting and third-party/supply-chain risk'). CORRECT FRAMING: there is no authoritative source for a 65% figure — it reads as fabricated precision. The accurate, defensible statement is qualitative: DORA is lex specialis for financial entities, so for firms in scope of both, DORA's ICT-risk-management and incident-reporting rules apply INSTEAD OF the corresponding NIS2 obligations (NIS2 Art. 4 / DORA Art. 1(2)). Reframe as 'DORA takes precedence for financial entities' rather than a made-up percentage, or drop the number.

**2. NIS2 fabricated instrument** · `Nis2.tsx` (lines 5, 9, 15, 16, 18)
Wrong: "Cooperation Group adopted common incident-reporting templates (26 May 2026)". Right: **no such event exists.** The real citable instrument is **Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 (17 Oct 2024)** defining "significant incident" thresholds. Remove the invented date or cite IR 2024/2690.

**3. Crosswalk fabricated milestone** · `Crosswalk.tsx` (line 54)
Wrong: countdown "Art. 50 AI-content marking (2 Dec 2026)". Right: **no 2 Dec 2026 milestone exists** in the AI Act; Art. 50 transparency/marking applies **2 Aug 2026**. Remove — it duplicates the first countdown.

**4. Crosswalk GPAI date — already in force** · `Crosswalk.tsx` (line 53)
Wrong: "EU AI Act GPAI + Art. 50 transparency enforceable (2 Aug 2026)". Right: **GPAI (Chapter V) obligations applied 2 Aug 2025** — live now. 2 Aug 2026 = high-risk (Annex III) + Art. 50 transparency. Drop "GPAI" from the 2026 pill.

**5. EU AI Act adoption date wrong** · `EUAIActGuide.tsx` (lines 111–113, 431–432)
Wrong: "European Parliament formally adopted the AI Act on July 12, 2024". Right: **Parliament adopted 13 March 2024, Council 21 May 2024; published in the OJ (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689) 12 July 2024; in force 1 August 2024.** No vote occurred on 12 July. Relabel that node "Published in the Official Journal".

**6. EU AI Act limited-risk deadline wrong** · `EUAIActGuide.tsx` (line 84)
Wrong: Limited Risk / Art. 50 transparency dated "August 2, 2025". Right: **Art. 50 transparency applies 2 August 2026.** Change the badge to 2 Aug 2026.

Wrong: "overlaps NIS2/DORA by ~65%". Drop the number everywhere.
